G25_ranking_by_scientific_defensibility.why: preserves a binary target close to the current scientific meaning, gives the ambiguous region declared semantics instead of hiding it, and can be frozen prospectively and confirmed on fresh identities

scientifically the most faithful description of stochastic families and already partly supported by the frozen checkpoint contract's Brier term, but it changes the loss, the metric set and the H1 framing, and costs the most compute
useful only as a component of D or E; alone it provably worsens the failing statistic
cheapest and least defensible; the amended threshold would sit just above the observed failure
outcome-dependent filtering that also damages H1 and H2 scope

consequences: the threshold would be selected after observing the failing result, which is the definition of a post-hoc gate amendment
V2 VALIDATION outcomes have also already been observed, so the amendment would be informed by both splits
it destroys the prospective-qualification claim for gate 7 and weakens the credibility of the other eight gates by association
any published threshold would visibly sit just above the observed failure, which is the least defensible possible justification
it does not change any label or any scientific fact; it only changes what the project declared acceptable in advance
options.description: raise the gate-7 threshold from 0.10 to some value >= 0.1113207547
options.name: RETROACTIVE_THRESHOLD_CHANGE

impacts.H2_scope: severely damaged if F9 is excluded

variants.exclude_F9: removes the only dynamic-obstacle family. F9 is a required family in the H1 requirement map and one of only two families carrying genuine measured H2 topology headroom (6 of the 7 headroom cells). It would gut H2 and narrow H1's declared scope.
variants.exclude_LINE: removes one of the two candidate topologies, which destroys candidate-conditioned learning outright. H1 is a candidate-conditioned claim; this is not a repair, it is abandonment.
variants.exclude_the_59_events: outcome-dependent filtering. The 59 are identified by their observed replica disagreement, so removing them conditions the dataset on the label outcome. It is only legitimate if a NEW prospectively frozen target explicitly defines such states as abstentions before they are observed.

options.compute: linear in R across all F8/F9 events
options.name: MORE_REPLICAS
options.operational_strengthening_vs_new_science: only the first variant would be mere operational strengthening, and it is the one that provably fails

variants.more_replicas_for_confidence_bound_robus: a NEW SCIENTIFIC TARGET as well, though it preserves a binary output. It changes how the label is derived.
variants.more_replicas_to_estimate_a_probabilisti: a NEW SCIENTIFIC TARGET, not operational strengthening. It changes what the label means.
variants.same_binary_all_success_target_and_same_: MATHEMATICALLY_COUNTERPRODUCTIVE. Disagreement probability 1 - p^R - (1-p)^R is strictly increasing in R for every p in (0,1), so more replicas strictly worsen the gate-7 statistic. This variant cannot work.

considerations.compatibility_with_H1: H1 is about selection improving episode task success; a calibrated probability supports selection at least as well as a binary label, but the H1 statement and its 0.08 threshold would need re-examination rather than silent reuse
considerations.decentralized_runtime: a probability is as deployable as a binary score for local ranking
considerations.evaluation_metrics: Brier score already appears in the frozen checkpoint selection contract, which is a point in this option's favour
considerations.loss: the frozen loss contract specifies BCE with logits and no class weighting; BCE against a soft target is a change to L_rec that must be prospectively frozen
considerations.replicas: materially more than 3 are needed for a usable estimate; 3 gives only {0, 1/3, 2/3, 1}
considerations.scientific_interpretation: directly expresses what the stochastic families actually produce, and makes the boundary region the signal rather than a quality defect

options.description: target P(success | local state, candidate topology, disturbance distribution) instead of a binary all-success label over three replicas
options.name: PROBABILISTIC_TARGET

considerations.abstain_semantics: would make the 59-type events a declared third class rather than silently dropped data, which is the only principled way to set them aside
considerations.parameter_selection: k, R and any confidence level must be motivated scientifically and frozen before generation, never chosen to make the current dataset pass
considerations.stability_gate: a successor stability gate would need to be defined on the new target, since a disagreement-frequency gate remains R-sensitive

options.description: a prospectively frozen robust binary target, for example a lower confidence bound on success probability, a predeclared k-of-R criterion, or robust-positive / robust-negative / ambiguous-abstain semantics
options.name: ROBUST_BINARY_TARGET_V3
